title: The Last Locker
premise: Oscar Villalobos, the only out kid in the dying farm town of Halstead, has survived high school by staying invisible — until she finds her late grandmother's recipe box hiding coded directions to an underground network that once smuggled queer kids out of hostile towns, and discovers her grandmother was its founder. When the network's last safe house is threatened by a vindictive school board member who knew grandma's secret, Oscar must come out of every closet at once: leading the network's final run while secretly competing in both the basketball championship nobody watches and the dangerous game of inheritance her grandmother left behind. In the end, Oscar wins neither trophy cleanly but wins something better — the town's memory rewritten, the last locker opened for good.
about_author: Ines Kavanagh grew up in a town small enough that everyone's business fit in one diner booth, and she writes about kids who refuse to shrink to match their zip codes. She lives with her wife, two dogs, and a recipe box of her own that contains exactly one secret.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A portrait of survival: Oscar navigates Halstead High's hallways, her closed locker a fortress, counting days until graduation. Her grandmother Abuela Rosa is her only ally, teaching her recipes and silence in equal measure. Beat: the fragile comfort of invisibility, and how much it costs.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. After Abuela Rosa's sudden death, Oscar inherits the recipe box and finds cards that aren't recipes: coordinates, names, dates, a key stamped with a locker number. The last card reads 'For when you're ready.' Beat: grief cracking open into vertigo — her grandmother had a whole hidden life.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The key opens a long-abandoned locker containing letters from decades of queer kids who passed through Halstead — and evidence Rosa ran an escape network called the Understory. School board member Dale Pruitt catches Oscar there, his eyes narrowing. Beat: inheritance becomes obligation.

chapters.title: Tryouts She Didn't Want
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. To stay close to the school and cover her investigation, Oscar joins the basketball team her grandmother once captained. Coach Reyes, an old friend of Rosa's, seems to know more than she says. First game looms. Beat: camouflage becoming community against her will.

chapters.title: What Pruitt Knows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Oscar and Pruitt. Pruitt, humiliated by Rosa decades ago, digs into school records hunting proof the network existed so he can bury it — and its beneficiaries. He finds a name that isn't Rosa's. Beat: the hunter revealed, old wounds driving new cruelty.

chapters.title: The Understory Rises
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following the recipe cards, Oscar finds the living remnants of the network: Coach Reyes, the diner owner, a retired librarian. They've kept one last safe house running for a scared sophomore, Marisol. Pruitt files to demolish it. Beat: Oscar stops being heir and becomes leader.

chapters.title: Outed at the Free Throw Line
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At a packed home game, Pruitt forces the issue — leaking Oscar's relationship with teammate June to the gymnasium crowd mid-game. Instead of collapsing, Oscar sinks the free throws through tears. Beat: the price of survival paid publicly, and found to be survivable.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The team, rallied around Oscar, reaches the county final — a game the town treats as trivial. Oscar plays it as cover: while the gym cheers, the network moves Marisol out under Pruitt's nose using the old routes. Beat: joy weaponized as misdirection; bittersweet victory.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. Pruitt corners Oscar in the locker room with demolition orders and a threat to expose everyone who helped. Oscar plays her grandmother's final card: recorded testimony proving Pruitt took Understory money years ago to stay quiet. The town hears everything. Beat: checkmate built from inherited courage.

chapters.title: Open
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, resolution. Spring: the safe house becomes a youth center bearing Rosa's name; Pruitt resigns in disgrace; Oscar and June walk the halls hand in hand. Oscar leaves Locker 114 unlocked, stocked with the letters, for whoever needs them next. Beat: memory inherited forward — survival turned into welcome.
